scope: Fix the three verified review findings R1/R2/R3 and regressions found while implementing their bounded-work design.
decision: The final package passes the targeted browser, performance, ownership and sampled-page acceptance gates and is ready for user retesting.

findingsConfirmedBeforeRepair: R1: seconds-long initial and paused bounded-layout policy scans on multiple real candidates.
R2: repeated media source capture/validation scans before the render slice, including fitting media with no installed correction.
R3: source text edited while paused leaves a stale unschedulable entry after resume in both display modes.
beforeScopeValidation.scope: Extension source-layout policy reads, bounded/media/anchor layout scheduling, and content-session resume reconciliation. The provider, cache proxy, collector rules and product settings are unchanged.

fixes.change: Share author stylesheet metadata and policy results only within a synchronous read pass; avoid serializing native grouping rule descendants; include source capture, contract validation and geometry in cooperative scheduling.
fixes.ownership: Validate each source contract afresh immediately before its write. Never reuse policy caches across writes, asynchronous yields, CSSOM changes or later passes.
fixes.limitBehavior: A limited read is explicitly incomplete and is not treated as an opaque stylesheet fallback. Optional geometry corrections are omitted or released without modifying author source styles.

fixes.change: Reconcile connected current/original source nodes before resumed observation and dispatch; restore/drop/recollect changed owners; preserve generation checks so old responses cannot overwrite new source.
fixes.coverage: Plain/rich text, link changes, node replacement/removal and already delivered hidden originals in both display modes; preserve page edits and source identities.

regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.problem: Bulk prevalidation would accept a later box after a synchronous custom-element callback changed its source during the first owned write.
regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.resolution: Keep fresh per-item validation immediately before each mutation.
regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.regression: A source callback collapses the next box; assert the extension never installs an owned correction on it.

regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.problem: The first per-owner capture/render slicing design measured some inner-row images after a sibling translation stretched the outer grid row. Only 12–16 of 24 needed constraints were installed.
regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.beforeRepairControl: The previous unbounded implementation installed all 24 media constraints but blocked a frame for 12150.6ms in the same native Chromium fixture.
regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.resolution: Capture a fixed cohort cooperatively before any of that cohort's text or layout writes. New responses join the next cohort. Keep fresh source checks for rendering and owned writes.
regressionsDetectedDuringRepair.regression: 6000-rule shared grid with 24 actual installed media constraints, paused sibling/author sizing changes and restoration; Chromium/Firefox and bilingual/replace all pass on the final artifact.

browserTests.mainSuiteCommand: PERF_FULL=1 npx playwright test e2e/regression.spec.ts e2e/lab.spec.ts e2e/firefox.spec.ts e2e/perf.spec.ts -g 'large stylesheet workload|layout stylesheet workload|layout write source guard|paused source resume|stylesheet layout regression|media policy regression|generic page layout|perf budget lab' --reporter=line
browserTests.additionalCommand: npx playwright test e2e/lab.spec.ts e2e/firefox.spec.ts -g '(motion|shared) policy regression: (bilingual|replace), paused=true, delivered=true' --reporter=line
includes: 24-card bounded, flex media, shared grid media and anchor stress fixtures
author stylesheet/container/scope/opaque-sheet and generic layout regression
sampled source inheritance, animations and shared ownership
all 8 existing performance gates, including 20k-node long tasks and both 30-navigation memory workloads

acceptance.build: Fresh Chromium and Firefox extension packages built; packaged script hashes match each other, tested output and all final private native probes.
acceptance.artifactChecks: Passed forbidden secret/development-file checks. Shipped permissions remain storage/contextMenus/activeTab/scripting with loopback required origins and optional HTTPS permission.
acceptance.finalCodeInspection: Checked final diff for read-cache lifetime, queue completion, pending-record preservation, per-write validation, generation checks and restoration. The two concrete implementation regressions above were corrected before final acceptance.
acceptance.goTests: not run; server code is unchanged

serialWorkloadMeasurements.method: Native Chromium MV3 extension with production background/relay, deterministic long Chinese translations, no CPU profiler and one browser workload at a time. Observe subsequent animation frames with performance.now after the action; exclude initial stylesheet parsing.
serialWorkloadMeasurements.mediaScope: The original flex workload exercises source capture/validation but does not require installed media corrections. The separate shared-grid public regressions assert all 24 real corrections and paused invalidation.

limits: Final Chromium acceptance loads the actual production MV3 extension. Firefox acceptance runs the built production content script on native Gecko through the repository harness; it does not establish full installed Firefox toolbar/background behavior.
Private native page probes grant only the selected site/provider origins in an isolated test copy to replace a missing activeTab toolbar gesture; shipped manifest permissions are unchanged.
Real-page samples cover the current viewport and nearby prefetch window. Indexed below-fold units are not equivalent to current in-flight requests or full-page visual coverage.
The reported GitHub page uses the authorized live MiMo provider. The other four page samples use deliberately length-varied Chinese mock translations to check rendering rather than model quality.

Restoration proofs for live samples cover the README or main subtree and its code nodes, with owned-node residue checked document-wide. The synthetic regressions check complete source fixtures, node order and page edits.
Live-page timing includes page work and CPU-profile overhead, so it is descriptive and is not mixed into the no-profiler stress comparison.
Extreme or unfinished cascade reads omit optional geometry corrections. They do not use a partial policy as proof that an important rule can mask author sizing.
The existing narrow Go commit-summary column can still wrap awkwardly with deliberately long mock translations; this lower-priority visual boundary is outside the three verified crash/resume fixes.
Earlier intermediate acceptance reports/packages are historical evidence. Only the final content-script hash and artifacts in this report are the delivery for this repair.

No browser-process or GPU crash was reproduced. The reproduced failure and before/after comparison are seconds-long main-thread blocking, alongside the independently verified paused-source scheduling defect.
git: Acceptance on 2026-10-09 used uncommitted sources based on a4b97669964d7f7a08698825b860d23f67a51b71. No push, branch rewrite or shipped permission expansion was part of the repair.

visualInspection.scope: Reported GitHub repository, golang/go, React homepage, Vue introduction and English Stripe payments, both display modes at 1920x1080; source screenshots and saved HTML used for comparison.
observations: Reported GitHub file rows, sidebar and navigation remain usable with live translated text in both display modes.
Vue code examples remain source code; translated documentation, image cards and tooltip content fit their columns.
English Stripe main content, image illustration, payment cards and fixed cookie bar remain present in both modes.
The Go commit summary retains its pre-existing narrow-column wrapping with length-varied mock translations; it is recorded as a remaining visual boundary.
